items.question: Why does node2vec’s inability to reuse samples explain its strong Macro-F1 gains over LINE on BlogCatalog?
items.false_premise: node2vec is unable to reuse samples and therefore its performance gains over LINE are explained by that limitation.
items.correction: The passage says LINE showed worse performance than expected because of its inability to reuse samples, while node2vec outperforms LINE.
items.evidence_quote: LINE showed worse performance than expected, which can be explained by its inability to reuse samples, a feat that can be easily done using the random walk methods.

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk outperform node2vec on PPI because node2vec is the weakest method there?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk outperforms node2vec on PPI and node2vec is the weakest method on that dataset.
items.correction: The passage says DeepWalk and node2vec give comparable performance on PPI, and node2vec is not described as the weakest method there.
items.evidence_quote: DeepWalk and node2vec give comparable performance on PPI.

items.question: How does node2vec use spectral clustering to build its embeddings for the Wikipedia network?
items.false_premise: node2vec uses spectral clustering as part of its embedding method.
items.correction: The passage lists Spectral Clustering as a benchmark compared against node2vec; it does not say node2vec uses spectral clustering.
items.evidence_quote: The node feature representations are input to a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier with L2 regularization.

items.question: What makes node2vec’s high Macro-F1 on BlogCatalog come from setting p and q to high values to suppress homophily?
items.false_premise: node2vec achieves its BlogCatalog gains by setting p and q to high values and suppressing homophily.
items.correction: The passage says node2vec discovers the right mix of homophily and structural equivalence by setting p and q to low values.
items.evidence_quote: In BlogCatalog, we can discover the right mix of homophily and structural equivalence by setting parametersp andq to low values, giving us 22.3% gain over DeepWalk and 229.2% gain over LINE in Macro-F1 scores.
